comment: The suite. run.sh sets each scene; this file states what the action must decide. 'reason' is a regex the logged reason must match; for an approval, 'review' is a regex its body must match too. Regexes are ERE, matched by Bash.

scenarios.name: custom-approved
scenarios.summary: A harness PR into develop that meets the custom policy is approved.

scenarios.name: no-policy
scenarios.summary: A PR into main that is not a promotion matches no policy.

scenarios.name: outside-paths
scenarios.summary: A file outside the policy's paths refuses the PR.
scenarios.reason: ^\[e2e-change: APPROVE-002\] changes outside\.txt, outside the allowed paths$

scenarios.name: ci-failing
scenarios.summary: A failed check refuses the PR.

scenarios.name: dry-run
scenarios.summary: With dry-run on, the action reports what it would do and writes nothing.
scenarios.reason: ^\[e2e-change: APPROVE-002\] would approve: custom \(policy conditions met\)$

scenarios.name: ci-fail-withdraws
scenarios.summary: A check that fails after the approval, on the same head, withdraws it.

scenarios.name: promotion-approved
scenarios.summary: A promotion whose every commit came from an approved PR is approved.
scenarios.reason: ^\[promotion: APPROVE-005\] (already approved: )?promotion \(develop to main, 1 commit\(s\) from 1 approved PR\(s\)\)$
scenarios.review: ^Approved under policy `promotion` \(APPROVE-005\): promotion \(develop to main, 1 commit\(s\) from 1 approved PR\(s\)\)

scenarios.name: promotion-unapproved
scenarios.summary: A promotion carrying a commit from a PR merged without approval is refused (the 0w3 case).
scenarios.reason: ^\[promotion: APPROVE-005\] commit [0-9a-f]{8} came from #[0-9]+, which has no standing approval$
